gaps.explanation: The governmental funds statement (trimmed p4) prints TOTAL RECEIPTS 7,282,051 and shows Sale of assets separately under other financing sources: General Fund 13,445 + Road Fund 3,480 = 16,925. The budgetary comparison schedules count the sale of assets inside 'Local' receipts. The General Fund schedule (p8) prints Local 815,228, while the combining General Fund statement (p5) prints 801,783 for the General Fund subfund; 815,228 - 801,783 = 13,445 (detail index 2). The Road Fund schedule (p9) prints Local 16,657, while p4 prints 13,177 for the Road Fund; 16,657 - 13,177 = 3,480 (detail index 33). 13,445 + 3,480 = 16,925 = 7,298,976 - 7,282,051. Every other fund agrees with p4. The schedules use a different receipt basis than the statement, so there is no fix.

On p4 the General Fund column nets the transfers between its own subfunds: Transfers - in 25,686, Transfers - out (661,937); Total 687,623 / (687,623). The combining General Fund statement (p5) and the General Fund budget schedule (p8) print them gross: General Fund Transfers - in 363,749 (detail index 21) + Emergency Management 30,000 (index 26), Total General Fund 393,749. 393,749 - 25,686 = 368,063, which is the transfers between General Fund subfunds that p4 eliminates. detail: 363,749 + 30,000 + Road Fund 661,937 (p9) = 1,055,686 = 687,623 + 368,063. The schedules record intra-General-Fund transfers gross, so there is no fix.

These are the same intra-General-Fund transfers. p4 prints General Fund Transfers - out (661,937) + Non-Major (25,686) = (687,623). p5 prints them gross: General Fund (30,000) (detail index 22) + Inheritance Tax Fund (1,000,000) (index 24), Total General Fund (1,030,000). Detail also has 911 Wireless Fund (25,686) from p6. 30,000 + 1,000,000 + 25,686 = 1,055,686, and 1,030,000 - 661,937 = 368,063 is netted out on p4. There is no fix.
